# Judith Chapter 16 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Judith 16 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/JDT_016_page_001.jpg

---

**THE SONG OF JUDITH**

**1** Judith said:

Strike up to my God with timbrels,
    sing to my Lord with cymbals;
sound for him a new psalm,
    exalt him and call upon his name.

**2** For the LORD is a God who crushes wars;
    he has pitched his camp among his people;
    he delivered me from the hand of those who pursued me.

**3** Assur came from the mountains of the north,
    he came with ten thousands of his army;
their multitude choked the wadis,
    and their cavalry covered the hills.

**4** He declared he would set fire to my territory
    and put my young men to the sword,
and dash my infants against the ground,
    and give my children up as plunder,
    and take my virgins as spoil.

**5** But the Lord Almighty brought them to nothing
    by the hand of a woman.

**6** For their champion fell not by the hand of young men,
    nor did the sons of Titans cut him down,
nor did tall giants fall upon him;
    but Judith daughter of Merari
    undid him with the beauty of her face.

**7** For she put off the garb of her widowhood
    to exalt the afflicted in Israel;
she anointed her face with precious oil,

**8** she bound her hair in a tiara,
    and put on a linen garment to deceive him.

**9** Her sandal ravished his eye,
    her beauty captured his soul —
    and the sword passed through his neck.

**10** The Persians trembled at her audacity,
    the Medes were confounded by her daring.

**11** Then my wretched ones raised a shout
    and my weak ones cried out;
the enemy was terror-stricken, they shrieked and fled.

**12** Sons of girls pierced them through,
    and like deserters' children wounded them;
they perished before the face of the LORD my God.

**13** I will sing to my God a new song:
O Lord, you are great and glorious,
    wondrous in strength and unconquerable.

**14** Let all your creation serve you,
    for you spoke, and they came to be;
you sent forth your spirit, and it fashioned them;
    and there is none that can resist your voice.

**15** For the mountains shall be shaken to their foundations along with the waters,
    and the rocks shall melt before your face like wax;
but to those who fear you
    you will still show mercy.

**16** For a fragrant offering is a small thing,
    and the fat of whole burnt offerings is less than nothing to you;
but whoever fears the Lord shall be great forever.

**17** Woe to the nations that rise against my people —
    the Lord Almighty will punish them on the day of judgment;
he will send fire and worms into their flesh,
    and they will weep in pain forever.

---

**18** When they came to Jerusalem, they worshiped God. When the people had been purified, they offered their whole burnt offerings, their freewill offerings, and their gifts.

**19** Judith dedicated to God all the possessions of Holofernes that the people had given her; and the canopy she had taken from his bedchamber she gave as a devoted thing to God.

**20** The people continued in festival before the sanctuary in Jerusalem for three months, and Judith remained with them.

**21** After these days every man went to his own inheritance, and Judith went to Bethulia and remained on her estate. For the rest of her life she was honored throughout all the land of Israel.

**22** Many men desired her, but no man knew her all the days of her life, from the day her husband Manasseh died and was gathered to his people.

**23** She grew even more renowned and she grew old in the house of her husband, living to one hundred and five years. She set her maidservant free. And she died in Bethulia, and they buried her in the cave of her husband Manasseh.

**24** The house of Israel mourned her for seven days. Before her death she distributed her property to all those nearest to her husband Manasseh and to those nearest to her own family.

**25** And no one ever again spread terror among the sons of Israel in the days of Judith, nor for a long time after her death.

---
*LOGOS notes: The song (vv. 1-17) is presented in formal verse layout. v. 5 — "woman" here renders thēleia (the female gender, more pointed than gynē — "woman"); the text emphasizes that it was a member of the female sex who did this, not merely "a woman." v. 6 — "Titans" preserved (Hellenistic Greek mythological reference) — the author signals that no superhuman male force could accomplish what Judith did. v. 14 — "spirit" rather than "breath" (pneuma) — LOGOS follows the divine-agency reading. v. 25 — the final verse is the book's epitaph. The silence after Judith's death is itself her legacy.*
